articles.title: Rochdale's Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield to Receive £20m for Community Improvements
articles.excerpt: The areas of Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield in Rochdale are set to benefit from £20m in government funding aimed at revitalising these historically overlooked communities over the next decade.
articles.content_html:
The communities of Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield in Rochdale are poised to receive nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising these areas, which have historically been overlooked for investment. The Rochdale Borough Council is expected to accept the Pride in Place funding of £19.6 million at a town hall meeting scheduled for August 25, 2026. This funding will be distributed over the next ten years, amounting to just under £2 million annually.

Currently, there is no definitive plan on how the funds will be allocated. However, early suggestions include tackling traffic congestion, improving parking facilities, creating new green spaces, enhancing local amenities, and expanding maternity services. To oversee the allocation of this funding, a Neighbourhood Board will be established, comprising local community representatives, Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, and the council’s regeneration lead, Councillor Daniel Meredith, with Laura Rodwell of the M6 Theatre group serving as chair.

The Neighbourhood Board will have until November 30, 2026, to submit a four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, which is necessary to unlock the funding. An initial grant of £150,000 has already been provided by the government to facilitate the formation of the board and the development of the plan.

Local residents have expressed a mix of skepticism and hope regarding the funding. Ken Whittle, a long-time resident, noted the area's lack of investment and called for improvements that would benefit children and the community. Another resident, Dinah Banks, highlighted the need for better healthcare services. MP Paul Waugh has conducted consultations with locals to gather their input on the desired improvements, ensuring that community voices will shape the future of the funding.
